facts.text: Fairview earned its name when Colonel Thomas Forster declared in 1797, “This is the fairest view I have seen yet,” and the name stuck.
The Sturgeon House, built around 1838, predates the Civil War by more than two decades and now serves as a museum on the National Register of Historic Places.
Stagecoaches once rattled through Fairview, making the township a key transit point in the early 19th century.
In 1844, the Erie Extension Canal opened, boosting Fairview’s role in regional trade and transportation.
The first saw‑mill and grist mill in Fairview, built by Forster in 1797 and finished in 1800, anchored the township’s earliest commerce.
Fairview’s German settlers, noted in 1871 for their honesty, industry, and perseverance, helped weave a lasting character into the community.
